Subject: Tri-region availability matrix for technical session (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Alex / Claire / Minoru —

Per our discovery call, the next step is a 60–90 minute technical session (SE + customer architects) to walk through integration specifics: network egress, token handling, and regional deployment options. Because we need engineers from US, EU and APAC on the call, I want to avoid the usual back-and-forth over timezones.

Quick constraints I recommend we use as anchors:
- Use UTC for scheduling to avoid daylight-savings confusion.
- Keep sessions between 13:00–20:00 UTC for best overlap across regions if possible.
- We will record and provide an incident-runbook template ahead of time.

Can each of you reply with your preferred windows (in UTC) and any hard blackout times? For context, a few example conversions:
- 13:00 UTC = 06:00 PT / 14:00 CET / 22:00 JST
- 17:00 UTC = 10:00 PT / 18:00 CET / 02:00 JST (next day)

Two administrative notes: EU is currently in CEST (DST) until late Oct, while Japan has no DST; converting all to UTC avoids off-by-one-hour mistakes when DST changes.

I’ll compile a small availability matrix and attach it as a CSV so we can pick the cleanest slot.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
